The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team** stands as a **landmark season** in Harvard and Ivy League basketball history, marking the program's modern renaissance and shattering decades of underdog status. Here's a comprehensive breakdown of everything notable about that team:

### Core Achievements & Significance
1.  **First NCAA Tournament Berth Since 1946:** Ended a **66-year drought**, the longest active NCAA tournament absence in Division I at the time. Harvard's previous appearance was in the *first-ever* NCAA tournament in 1939 (finishing 3rd).
2.  **First Ivy League Championship Since 1984:** Won the Ivy League title **outright** with a 12-2 conference record (previous title was shared in 1984). This was Harvard's first *outright* title since 1955.
3.  **Highest-Profile Victory Ever:** Achieved a #12 seed in the NCAA Tournament (East Region), the **highest seed ever for an Ivy League team** at that time (surpassing Penn's #6 seeds). This reflected the committee's recognition of the Ivy's strength.
4.  **Program Transformation Catalyst:** Cemented Coach Tommy Amaker's rebuild (started in 2007) and proved Harvard could compete nationally, paving the way for sustained success (5 NCAA bids in the next 8 years).

### Key Personnel
*   **Head Coach:** **Tommy Amaker** (4th season). Former Michigan "Fab Five" member and Michigan head coach. His leadership, recruiting, and defensive schemes were fundamental to the turnaround.
*   **Star Players:**
    *   **Keith Wright (Sr, F):** **Ivy League Player of the Year (POY)**, 1st Team All-Ivy, NCAA All-Regional Honorable Mention. Stats: 14.8 PPG, 7.4 RPG, 1.6 BPG. Dominant low-post presence, elite rebounder/defender.
    *   **Kyle Casey (Jr, F):** 1st Team All-Ivy, Ivy League scoring leader (15.7 PPG), elite rebounder (6.7 RPG). Physical, versatile forward.
    *   **Laurent Rivard (So, G):** Sharpshooting guard (41.9% 3PT), 2nd Team All-Ivy. Key perimeter threat and floor spacer (11.8 PPG).
    *   **Brandon Smith (Sr, G):** Steady point guard (10.2 PPG, 3.1 APG), 3rd Team All-Ivy. Floor general and defensive leader.
    *   **Christian Webster (Sr, G):** Veteran leader (10.8 PPG), 3rd Team All-Ivy. Clutch shooter.
    *   **Other Key Contributors:** Kyle Singler (Sr, F - defensive specialist), Jonah Travis (So, C), Kenyatta Smith (So, F/C - emerging shot-blocker), Travis Webster (So, G), Steve Moundou-Missi (Fr, F).
*   **Notable Absence:** **Siyani Chambers (Fr, G)** - A highly touted recruit, he suffered a season-ending knee injury in the 2nd game (Nov 14 vs. MIT), forcing others like Smith and Travis Webster into larger roles.

### Season Highlights & Performance
*   **Record:** **26-5 Overall** (12-2 Ivy League). This set the program record for wins in a season (since broken).
*   **Ivy League Dominance:**
    *   Won 11 of their last 12 conference games.
    *   Clinched the title with a **77-67 victory over arch-rival Yale** at Lavietes Pavilion on March 2nd (Senior Night).
    *   Key wins included sweeps of traditional powers Princeton and Penn (including a 72-45 beatdown at The Palestra).
*   **Non-Conference Strength:**
    *   Notable wins: Vermont (82-67), Boston University (74-54), St. John's (73-66 - *first win vs. a non-conference BCS AQ team since 1963*), at #25/24 Florida State (53-51 - *program's first true road win vs. a ranked team*).
    *   Losses: Early setback to MIT (due to Chambers injury), close losses to UMass (70-61) and Rhode Island (73-71).
*   **Defensive Identity:** The team was defined by **elite defense** under Amaker:
    *   Led the Ivy League in Scoring Defense (58.2 PPG), Field Goal % Defense (38.4%), 3PT % Defense (31.2%), and Blocks (4.6 BPG).
    *   Ranked **Top 25 nationally in multiple defensive categories**, including scoring defense (19th).
*   **Academic Excellence:** Multiple players named to Ivy League All-Academic Teams, embodying the "student-athlete" ideal. Wright and Casey were also strong academic performers.

### The NCAA Tournament Experience
*   **Opponent:** #5 seed **Arizona Wildcats** (Russell Westbrook's alma mater, coached by Sean Miller).
*   **Game (March 16, 2012 - Jacksonville, FL):** Harvard played **competitively for 30 minutes**, trailing only 38-34 at halftime. Wright (13 pts, 7 reb) and Rivard (12 pts) led the charge. However, Arizona's superior athleticism and depth took over in the 2nd half. Final Score: **Arizona 74, Harvard 51**.
*   **Legacy Moment:** Despite the loss, the game was a cultural moment. Sean McDonough's ESPN call – *"Harvard, hanging around... Harvard, hanging around... WAITING TO SEE IF HARVARD CAN BEAT ARIZONA... IT'S STILL POSSIBLE!"* – became iconic, symbolizing the changing landscape of college basketball and Harvard's arrival. It proved they *belonged* on the big stage.

### Why This Season Was Revolutionary
*   **Broken Stigma:** Shattered the perception of the Ivy League as a basketball afterthought and Harvard as a perpetual academic powerhouse with weak athletics. Proved elite academics and elite basketball could coexist.
*   **Recruiting Catalyst:** Elevated Harvard's national recruiting profile significantly, attracting future high-major transfers and top academics/athletes.
*   **Foundation for Sustained Success:** Directly led to Harvard becoming a consistent Ivy League powerhouse and NCAA contender (NCAA bids in 2013, 2014, 2015, 2017; shared or outright Ivy titles 5 times between 2011-12 and 2016-17).
*   **National Recognition:** Garnered unprecedented national media coverage for an Ivy League team, featured on ESPN, Sports Illustrated, and major newspapers well beyond the tournament.

### Lasting Legacy
The 2011-12 Harvard Crimson are remembered not just for their record or tournament appearance, but for **fundamentally altering the trajectory of the program and challenging perceptions of what's possible for an Ivy League basketball team**. They were the proof of concept for Tommy Amaker's vision and ignited a sustained period of excellence that continues to define Harvard basketball today. They transformed from historical footnotes into a nationally respected program overnight. The image of the team celebrating its Ivy title on the Lavietes court and then holding up the NCAA bid banner remains one of the most iconic moments in modern Ivy League sports history.
